statement: There is an explicit family of ordinary local tripod points whose values at t-2 fail restricted-product admissibility at every modulus greater than one, while every finite-character cup-invariant sum is locally finite and zero after every finite number-field base change. The data satisfy restriction and norm-of-restriction identities; the exceptional rational primes have Dirichlet density zero. Thus characterwise reciprocity and these finite-base identities do not imply the admissibility hypothesis in D.27.
where_proved: sections/D_unrestricted_reciprocity_extension.tex, D.29; recursively completely split primes, convergent local products, exact valuation and cusp-avoidance computations, approximation by finite principal products, and global Brauer reciprocity
depends_on: D.27 for the precise comparison with Poitou-Tate; Milne2020 CFT Chapter III Proposition3.6 and Lemma3.7, Chapter V Theorem3.23, Chapter VIII Theorem4.2; Hensel's lemma
manuscript_passages: 149; manuscript pp.27-31,62v-63; scans56,59-63,126-127; prompt PartD1-D4 and the proposed canonical translated-Kummer route
doubtful_reading: No new manuscript reading. This is a counterexample to a proposed implication between arithmetic conditions on local tuples, not to a section assertion.
notes: Root independently read the complete proof, opened the three primary Milne loci, and reran the exact finite certificate before integration. The tuple is not asserted to arise from a section, to satisfy global completed t and1-t Kummer conditions, or to satisfy all accessible-neighbourhood conditions. Character-dependent finite pairing support is distinguished from membership in the restricted product. Real values are separately fixed at1; no real convergence of the positive products is claimed. Norm compatibility means only norm of restriction equals the degree power. The canonical program and output are in code/D_unrestricted_reciprocity_checks.py and .json; old audit copies are explicitly superseded. D1-D4 remain unresolved.
